hero.subtitle: From your home to your workplace, from parking solutions to the field — we facilitate the electric vehicle experience with certified AC chargers, cables, and accessories.

wallbox.name: AC Mobile Chargers
wallbox.subtitle: 22-3.7kW Portable Chargers

faq.q: What is the difference between 7 kW and 11 kW and 22 kW?
faq.a: Powered by 7 kW single-phase connection and sufficient for overnight charging; fully charges a typical EV in 6-8 hours. Requires 11 kW and 22 kW three-phase connection; same vehicle with 22 kW will fill up in 2-3 hours. If your vehicle's AC charging acceptance power is 11 kW, getting a 22 kW device does not provide additional speed; check your vehicle manual before purchasing.

faq.q: Is the Type 2 connector compatible with all electric vehicles?
faq.a: Yes. All electric vehicles sold in the European market (including Tesla Model 3/Y), Chinese BYD and MG models, Korean and Japanese EVs use the IEC 62196-2 (Type 2) standard on the AC side. Our Bemis Wallbox devices are in this standard; no additional adapters are required.

faq.q: What is dynamic load balancing?
faq.a: While other devices connected to the same mains line draw high power (air conditioner, oven, heat pump), the wallbox automatically lowers the charging power and prevents the fuse from blowing. In multiple wallbox installations, it allocates the total available power between the devices in a balanced way. It is a critical feature that reduces both security and infrastructure cost.

faq.q: What does IP65 protection class mean?
faq.a: IP65 indicates that the device is completely closed to dust (6) and resistant to water jets from all directions (5). Our Bemis Wallboxes are in this class; no additional protective cabin is required for outdoor parking, balconies and outdoor installations.

faq.q: Installation included
faq.a: The price of the device does not include installation. Our authorized dealer makes an exploration and makes a separate offer for line drawing, cabling and fuse board works. The average installation cost varies between 5,000-15,000 TL; it is determined according to the existing infrastructure.

faq.q: Does the portable charger operate from a normal outlet?
faq.a: Yes. Our Bemis Mobile Charger products work with both standard 16a single-phase sockets and 32a industrial type CEE sockets. Pro models offer charging from a three-phase 32a socket to 22 kW; Mini models are suitable for household sockets with 3.6 kW.

wallbox.description: Portable AC chargers that do not require installation — from the standard outlet or CEE socket to the Type 2 vehicle socket. Flexible charging solution for road, camp and backup scenarios with single-phase 2.3 – 7.4 kW and three-phase 11 – 22 kW options.

portable.name: AC Charging Cables
portable.subtitle: Type 2 · Mode 3

faq.q: What is the difference between Mini Mobile and Pro Mobile?
faq.a: Mini Mobile: 3.6 kW single phase, compact size, ideal for home/travel. Pro Mobile: adjustable power from 7-22 kW, three-phase support, for professional use. In the Pro model, the current limit (6A-32A) can be set on the screen; the power is constant on the Mini.

faq.q: What happens if the mobile charger is submerged?
faq.a: Protection class IP54 is suitable for use in rain, but the product should not be under water. After the device case is wet, it should be wiped with a dry cloth before plugging in. In case of flooding, do not operate without taking it to the authorized service.

faq.q: Can it be used as a spare on the trip?
faq.a: Yes, this is exactly what portable chargers are for. In places such as hotels, camping areas, holiday villages, where there is no DC/AC charging point, charging is done from the existing sockets. It is stored in its bag, weighing an average of 4-6 kg.

faq.q: How do I choose between mobile charging and fixed wallbox?
faq.a: If you park your car in the same place every day, the fixed wallbox is faster, safer and more economical in the long run. If you travel frequently or switch between multiple venues, a mobile charger is a more flexible solution. It is also a common choice to take both.

faq.q: How many meters should the AC charging cable be?
faq.a: We see that 5 meters of cable is sufficient in most cases: it is ideal if the distance of the car charging socket to the wall does not exceed 3-4 meters when parking. If your garage/parking layout is different, there are 7.5 m or 10 m options. The longer the cable, the heavier and more rigid it is; unnecessarily long selection makes it difficult to carry.

portable.description: Mode 2 and Mode 3 charging cables with Type 2 standard. It is designed for long-lasting use in single and three-phase, 16a – 32a current classes with IEC 62196 / IEC 61851 compliant, halogen-free outer sheath and high-current Type 2 connector.

cables.name: V2L / C2L Adapters
cables.subtitle: Vehicle-to-Load & Charger-to-Load Discharge & Battery Charge

faq.q: What is the difference between Type 2 and Type 1?
faq.a: Type 1 (SAE J1772) is used on North American and older Asian vehicles, supporting single-phase up to 7.4 kW. Type 2 (IEC 62196-2) is the European standard and supports up to 22 kW of three-phase. Almost all new EVs in the Turkish market use Type 2. The older versions of the Tesla Model S/X were the Type 1; the newer Teslas are the Type 2.

faq.q: How do I choose between 16a and 32a cable?
faq.a: 16a cables withstand up to 3.7 kW in one phase and 11 kW in three phases. 32a cables have a capacity of 7.4 kW in one phase and 22 kW in three phases. The higher current the wallbox or vehicle can draw, choose the cable according to that current; if there is a bottleneck in the cable, the charging speed decreases.

faq.q: Does cable selection vary by vehicle brand?
faq.a: Since the connector type is standardized (Type 2 in almost all European markets), the choice of cable is brand-independent. The only difference is the AC charging acceptance capacity of each vehicle: if you take a 22 kW cable to a vehicle that accepts 11 kW, it will not flow much power, only safety.

faq.q: Does the three-phase cable work with my vehicle?
faq.a: Yes, the three-phase cable also supports single-phase charging. If your vehicle is single-phase, the cable automatically runs in single-phase and is limited to 7.4 kW. The three-phase cable ensures that you do not make unnecessary changes if you buy a three-phase vehicle in the future.

faq.q: What does V2L (Vehicle to Load) do?
faq.a: V2L allows you to use your vehicle's battery as a portable power source. The adapter plugs into the vehicle socket and outputs a standard 220V output. You can operate refrigerators, projectors, small devices in cases such as camping, outdoor activities, power outages. The energy comes from the vehicle's battery.

cables.description: Adapters that convert the vehicle's battery (V2L) or charger (C2L) into an external power supply. Compatible with Type 2 inputs and schuko / Cee outputs and V2L-supported vehicles such as Hyundai, Kia, MG, BYD, Ssangyong and Skywell — for camping, workshop and emergency scenarios.

v2l-c2l.name: Overtime & Combination
v2l-c2l.subtitle: Extension Cables, Converters & Combination Boxes
v2l-c2l.badge: How do I use the AC Wallbox charger in my home?

faq.q: What does C2L (Charger to Load) do?
faq.a: The C2L adapter converts electricity drawn from the Type 2 socket of the AC charging station into a standard Schuko (household) or CEE (industrial) socket. Thus, a Type 2 charging point can be used not only for vehicle charging — but also as a 220V/380V output for workshop, event space or temporary installation. The energy comes from the charger, it does not use your vehicle's battery.

faq.q: What is the difference between V2L and C2L?
faq.a: The only difference is where the energy comes from: V2L takes the energy FROM the vehicle (the vehicle's battery is the source) — your vehicle becomes a mobile power source. C2L receives energy from the CHARGER UNIT (Type 2 charger source) — it converts a charging point into a conventional outlet. The two serve different purposes; with the Combi Set you can get both adapters in one package.

faq.q: Which vehicles support V2L?
faq.a: Vehicles such as Hyundai Ioniq 5/6, Kia EV6/EV9, Genesis GV60, Ssangyong (KGM) Torres EVX, MG ZS EV / MG4, BYD Atto 3/Seal / Han, Skywell ET5 support ex-factory V2L. Our Bemis V2L adapters are manufactured in the socket pin array of these manufacturers — mark the variant that suits your vehicle when selecting the product (Hyundai/Kia/Ssangyong, MG, BYD/Skywell). Tesla vehicles are not supported as standard.

faq.q: How much power can be drawn from the V2L adapter?
faq.a: Depends on the V2L power of the vehicle. Hyundai/Kia up to 3.6 kW (16a) on most models, BYD and MG up to 2.2 kW (10a), some newer models up to 7.2 kW. Our Bemis V2L adapters transmit the output power of the vehicle safely; it does not exceed the limit of your vehicle. Single, double, and triple-socket versions share the same total power.

faq.q: Does the use of V2L damage the battery?
faq.a: No. V2L is a mode of use prescribed by the manufacturer; the battery management system (BMS) controls the depth of discharge. Most vehicles turn off automatically when the battery level drops to 20% in V2L mode. Continuous use does not affect battery life.

faq.q: Is the charging cable extension safe?
faq.a: Our Bemis extension cables are manufactured to the same standards (IEC 62196-2, 32a copper conductor) as the original cable. Class IP54 connection sections are protected against water. Third-party low-quality extensions may pose a fire risk; use only certified products.

v2l-c2l.description: Extension cables and Ceenorm converters that carry existing charging equipment to different outlet types and distances. Combination solutions designed for single and three-phase 16a – 32a transitions.

converters.name: AC & DC Charging Unit Equipment
converters.subtitle: Type 2, CCS2 Socket, Unit Socket, Holder

faq.q: In which cases is it necessary to use an extension?
faq.a: If the place where the vehicle is parked is far from the wall where the wallbox is located, if the parking entrance area is long, if the load point is far in mobile environments such as camping, extension is used. Additional extension is unnecessary if your standard 5 m cable is sufficient; each port is an additional point of sensitivity.

faq.q: Can different connector types be made compatible with the converter?
faq.a: Yes, we have adapters for common conversions such as Type 1 to Type 2, CEE socket to Type 2, Type 2 to Schuko. But there is no conversion between DC and AC; each system operates separately. The transducers receive the power limit relative to the low side.

faq.q: How many meters can the extension cable be?
faq.a: The total cable length (original + extension) should not exceed 15 meters for 22 kW in one phase and 25 meters for 11 kW in three phases. At longer distances, power drops and heating increases due to cable resistance. Fixed wiring is recommended for installations requiring long distances.

faq.q: Which socket types are common in Turkey?
faq.a: Schuko (standard Turkish socket), 16a industrial CEE blue socket, 32a CEE red three-phase socket are common in home charging. Type 2 is standard in public AC points. CCS2 (most common) and CHAdeMO (Nissan/old vehicles) appear in DC fast charging.

faq.q: What is included in the Charging Unit Equipment category?
faq.a: Professional equipment used in charging station installations includes: AC and DC charging sockets (Type 2, CCS2), wired and wireless versions, socket covers, locking mechanisms, optional communication modules and spare parts that can be integrated into the charger. Uses OEM manufacturers and service.

faq.q: What is the difference between a DC charging socket and an AC charging socket?
faq.a: AC sockets (Type 2) conduct a maximum of 22 kW alternating current and are of simple structure. DC sockets (CCS2) deliver 50-350 kW of direct current, including liquid cooling, temperature sensor and thicker conductors. DC sockets are 3-4 times heavier and require special installation.

faq.q: What is required for an operator who wants to install a charging station?
faq.a: Transformer connection or sufficient subscription power, OCPP 1.6J/2 .0.1 supported chargers, a CPO software for billing/management, EMRA license or dealer agreement are required. Our Bemis B2B team supports turnkey installation from site survey to hardware supply.

faq.q: What is a CCS2 socket?
faq.a: Combined Charging System 2 (CCS2) is the DC fast charging standard of the European market. It is a combined design with two additional DC pins attached under the Type 2 AC connector; both AC and DC charging can be done from the same vehicle socket. It supports power from 50-350 kW.

faq.q: Is replacement of spare socket or cable possible?
faq.a: Yes. The cables and sockets of our Bemis chargers are of modular design; in case of wear or damage, our authorized service can quickly replace them. We manage inventory for special parts such as CCS2 liquid-cooled cables.

faq.q: Why do I need an RFID card?
faq.a: The RFID card provides user authorization at the charging station — someone you don't want can't use the device. It is used to track who charges how much with which vehicle in corporate/workplace installations. You can do the same job with the mobile application in OCPP supported stations.

accessories.name: DC Charging Units
accessories.subtitle: 40-200kWFast Charging Units

faq.q: Why buy a charging cable case?
faq.a: Carrying the mobile charger without a bag in the trunk of the vehicle will batter both the cable and the interior trim of the vehicle. The bag insulates the moisture in the cloth, protects the plugs from crushing and provides practical use during travel. Bags may be standard in our Pro Mobile products and optional in others.

faq.q: Are Bemis accessories compatible with other brands?
faq.a: Since connector standards (Type 2, CCS2, RFID Mifare) are universal, our Bemis accessories are compatible with all electric vehicles and charging stations that use standard Type 2 / CCS2 connectors. Brand-specific features (firmware lock, registered card system) are specified in the document, if any.

faq.q: How to order spare accessories?
faq.a: The request can be sent directly from the contact form with the product code, our sales team guides the dealer. For bulk ordering operators, integrated ordering is possible with API via OEM account. Parts that are not in our stock are supplied within 2-4 weeks.

faq.q: What should I do if the RFID card is lost?
faq.a: When the card is lost, it can be deactivated from the admin panel or by notifying our sales team. A new card match is completed in 5 minutes. The risk of unauthorized use with the lost card is negligible because each card is connected to the device recording system.

faq.q: What is the difference between DC charging and AC charging?
faq.a: In AC charging, electricity flows to the vehicle as alternating current and the internal converter converts it to direct current; therefore, it is limited to 22 kW. In DC charging, the conversion is done inside the station and the direct current flows directly to the battery; it can go up to 50-350 kW. Conclusion: With DC, an EV reaches 80% in 20-40 minutes, while 6-8 hours are required in AC.

dc-units.name: DC Charging Units
dc-units.subtitle: 40-200kW Fast Charging Units

faq.q: What is the difference between DC charging and AC charging?
faq.a: In AC charging, electricity reaches the vehicle as alternating current and the on-board converter rectifies it; this caps the rate at 22 kW. In DC charging, the conversion happens inside the station and direct current flows straight into the battery, reaching up to 50-350 kW. The result: an EV hits 80% in 20-40 minutes on DC, while AC needs 6-8 hours.

faq.q: How many vehicles can BEVDC models charge at the same time?
faq.a: BEVDC-40 is single-socket and delivers 40 kW to a single vehicle. BEVDC-80, BEVDC-120, BEVDC-160 and BEVDC-200 are dual-socket; total power can be split between two vehicles simultaneously. For example, the BEVDC-200 can deliver 100 kW to each of two vehicles at the same time, or 200 kW to a single vehicle (if the vehicle supports it).

faq.q: What is required for DC charger installation?
faq.a: DC units require a 3-phase 380-480V grid connection, a transformer or high-power subscription (200-400 kVA) for BEVDC-120 and above, a ground-fixing pad, sufficient airflow for cooling, and an Ethernet or 4G line for OCPP communication. The Bemis B2B team manages the whole process from site survey to commissioning.

faq.q: Which BEVDC model fits my fleet?
faq.a: BEVDC-40 is enough if your fleet vehicles average 50-60 kWh batteries and stay urban. For long-haul commercial fleets or quick-turn taxi/courier operations, BEVDC-120 reaches 80% in 30 minutes. For high-traffic public stations, BEVDC-160/200 is recommended; two vehicles charge quickly at the same time.

faq.q: What is needed to open a public DC charging point?
faq.a: Under EMRA's charging service regulation, you need a licence or authorisation, an OCPP-capable device, integration with the EPVIS system, and a billing/payment stack (Bemis CPO software or a 3rd-party platform). Investment size ranges between 1-3 million TL; our B2B team supports roadmap preparation.
